A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CMIC and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting a reliable comparison. All 20 pages of each were inspected, including v1's checklist and v4's technical appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments on Kodak, Tecnick and CLIC, including rate-distortion results, complexity measurements, component ablations and visual analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original compression results and adds experiments on throughput, cluster count, entropy-model alternatives and training stability, including appendix results.

M1.justification: Figure 2 changes the reported block order in stages 2–5 from CAM-before-attention to attention-before-CAM. Algorithm 1 also corrects clustering iterations to use updated tentative centroids rather than repeatedly using fixed centroids. The core permutation, prompting and loss mechanisms remain. The PDFs do not establish whether these revisions reflect implementation changes or corrections to its description.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Flickr2W training data and the Kodak, Tecnick and CLIC professional validation benchmarks for natural-image compression. The added ablations and visual examples stay within this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated WeConvene and S2CFormer baselines. Figure 7 extends ERF comparisons to these methods and MLIC++. The structure ablation removes Swin Transformer and introduces CAM-only, while Appendix A.2 adds a comparison using Zhang et al. (2024)'s reported RD curves. These substantially expand and revise the comparisons.

E3.justification: The principal training settings remain, but v4 substantially expands the evaluation design with throughput measured on 256×256 patches at batch size 8, fixed-query per-image ERFs, and controlled entropy-model substitutions, including matching FTIC's T-CA model. Figure 6 also replaces the reported CLIC MS-SSIM comparison with a Kodak comparison; these are different evaluation conditions.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablation, v4 adds cluster-count sensitivity, active-centroid statistics, component overhead measurements, entropy-model ablations, matched-entropy comparisons and seed-dependent convergence analysis. Per-image ERFs and reconstruction comparisons extend v1's averaged ERFs and cluster masks (Section 4.5 and Appendices A.3–A.8).

E5.justification: v1 reports no specific seeds or repeated-run results. v4 first presents separate convergence curves for seeds 1024 and 16 in Figure 18 and reports descriptive variance of active-cluster counts in Table 5. This adds limited variability reporting, without confidence intervals or significance tests for the headline RD comparisons.

E6.justification: CMIC's headline BD-rates and Table 2 remain unchanged. However, Table 1 changes MLIC++'s Kodak/Tecnick/CLIC entries from -11.97/-15.13/-12.08% to -13.42/-16.73/-13.94%. Numerous baseline, throughput, cluster-count and entropy-ablation results are added. MS-SSIM findings are replaced under different dataset conditions, and the stated memory reduction versus MambaIC is corrected from 57% to 78% using unchanged memory measurements.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2.2 newly asserts permutation equivariance and translation invariance of the clustering assignments and contrasts these properties with spatially anchored clustering. These are limited mathematical property claims without formal proofs. The principal SSM, prompting and rate-distortion equations remain equivalent; the appendix's SCCTX equations mainly elaborate the existing computation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that content-based token reordering and dictionary prompting improve Mamba's global modeling efficiently, and both claim state-of-the-art compression with identical headline BD-rates. v4 foregrounds efficiency advantages already discussed in v1 and renames the components, while retaining the core scientific contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive interpretations of adaptive centroid activation, shared semantic prototypes, per-block codebooks, ERF artifacts and the limited usefulness of global modeling inside the entropy model. It also acknowledges biased gradients from nondifferentiable clustering. Conversely, v1's explicit ordering limitation and hierarchical-sorting future work disappear; Appendix A.10 documents ordering without retaining that limitation discussion.

D1.justification: v4 adds VTM commands, detailed entropy and basic-block descriptions, first-batch centroid initialization, stable-sorting details and an explicit distinction between EMA centroid updates and gradient-trained prompts. It removes v1's five-slice specification and disclosure that MambaIC was reproduced by the authors. Code release remains prospective, changing from release upon acceptance to the less specific 'later.'

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A.2 substantially expand positioning against prior clustering-based compression, especially Zhang et al. (2024). v4 also introduces explicit VQ-VAE inspiration and broader token-reordering connections, alongside additional INR, region-adaptive and Mamba compression literature. This changes the account of relevant predecessors beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The introduction and method explanations are extensively rewritten around content awareness and codebooks, and the prompting discussion is reordered. Content-Adaptive Mamba and Token Aggregation become Content-Aware Mamba and Token Permutation. The limitations section and NeurIPS checklist are removed, while technical material is organized into ten appendix subsections.

P2.justification: RD panels are regrouped and recolored, tables are reformatted and expanded, and the averaged ERF display gains comparators. Existing cluster masks are reordered and annotated with centroid identities and activation ratios. New per-image ERFs, reconstruction grids, convergence plots, block diagrams and ablation tables substantially expand the visual presentation; the entropy schematic is also repeated in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens support for the retained method. The matched FTIC-entropy comparison and entropy, overhead, cluster-count and convergence studies address important gaps in v1 concerning attribution, efficiency and clustering stability. Detailed implementation documentation and direct engagement with prior clustering-based compression improve reproducibility and assessment of novelty. Removing the explicit limitation discussion and MambaIC reproduction disclosure reduces transparency, and headline uncertainty remains unreported, but these losses are outweighed by the substantive gains.
